Subject: Quick recap from today + benchmarking ask

Thanks again for the call today — useful discussion. A few points I wanted to capture so we have a concrete scope for the benchmark run: 

- Goal: validate real-world latency (p95/p99) and steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) for our clinical summarization workload. We need numbers vs the hyperscaler endpoints we currently use (HyperScaleNet and CloudGiant) so procurement can compare unit economics and tail latency risk.
- Workload: ~1.2k requests/day, avg 420 tokens output, 90% < 800 tokens, peak bursts up to 2.5k concurrent.
- Success metrics: p95 < 250ms for short requests (<=128 tokens), p99 < 600ms for long requests (>=512 tokens); sustained tokens/sec >= 18k on a single node equivalent, or clear scaling profile.

Action: can you share a proposed AB test matrix (models, sequence lengths, quantization, batching) and the minimal config we need to run in our test account? Also interested in how Redwood’s prefix/KV caching and continuous batching would be measured in this context.

Tom
Tom Riley
SRE Lead, Atlas Health

Tom — thanks, this is super clear. Below is a compact AB plan and the minimal artifacts we need to run a comparable bench: 

Summary AB matrix (initial):
- Redwood-hosted (Redwood API, model: redwood-v2-large, quantized FP16/INT8 where applicable)
- HyperScaleNet-hosted (their recommended LLM variant, default FP16)
- CloudGiant-managed endpoint (default config they suggested)

Test vectors & slices:
- Short (<=128 tokens), Mid (129-512), Long (>512 up to 800) -- sample 1k requests per slice
- Burst test: ramp to 2.5k concurrent over 60s, hold 3 min, measure p95/p99 and error rate
- Steady-state tokens/sec: sustained run for 10 minutes with arrival rate tuned to keep CPU/GPU util ~70%

What we measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model outputs per second, 95th/99th tail error rate, unit cost per 1k tokens (including infra), and CPU/GPU utilization.

Minimal artifacts we need from you:
- Small dataset (50 representative prompts + expected length distribution) OR permission to mirror a sanitized sample set.
- Temporary test credentials (read-only) or whitelisted IP for our probe runner; alternatively we can run from your CloudBench partner if you prefer.
- Target Hyperscaler endpoint URLs + any rate limits.

Engineering notes / Redwood differentiators to track during runs:
- Continuous batching behavior and latency distribution under mixed seq lengths
- Prefix/KV cache hit patterns for repeated patient prompt prefixes
- Automatic fallback to lighter model variant when queueing breaches SLOs

Next steps (proposal):
1) We send a detailed benchmark plan and estimate (Marcus + Jordan to own by Mon 11/12).
2) Atlas provides sample prompts and test endpoint access by Tue 11/13.
3) Run AB tests Wed–Thu (11/14–11/15), initial readout Fri 11/16.

I attached a simple workbook with the matrix — will follow up with a more formal lab plan.

Thanks,

Adding the engineering perspective — a few clarifications and what I'll prepare: 

Clarifications needed from Atlas:
- Are you OK with us running traffic from Redwood-managed runners, or do you prefer CloudBench (bench@cloudbench.io) to execute to avoid routing complexity?
- Do you want HTTP streaming enabled for long responses (this changes p95 patterns)?

What I'll deliver: 
- A harness (JMeter + custom tokenizer) that measures p50/p95/p99 and emits tokens/sec per second samples.
- A config matrix: batch sizes, max_wait_ms (continuous batching knob), KV cache enabled/disabled, and model quantization options.
- Baseline run that disables caching and batching (to capture raw kernel perf) + production-like run with batching/caching enabled so you can see the delta.

Important test note: for fair hyperscaler comparison we need to align GPU types and model variants where possible; when not possible we’ll normalize by tokens/sec per GPU vCPU equivalence in the readout.

I'll aim to have the harness and preliminary matrix uploaded to the shared drive by EOD Tue (11/13).

-Marcus
